newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Human pays lower dividend, sees profit up.
newsitem.headline: Human pays lower dividend, sees profit up.

text.p: Shareholders in Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Human Rt have decided to spend 20 percent of Human's unconsolidated after-tax profit of 676.5 million forints on dividend payments.
The amount represents a 3.56 percent dividend or 35.6 forints per share, against a six percent dividend a year ago.

Company financial director Gyula Rudolf told shareholders that Human's 1997 plan sees a profit of 790 million forints and also said that the company's first quarter performance was in harmony with the year's targets.
"In the first quarter of the year Human Rt's operation was in line with plans," Rudolf said. "It is a realistic target to meet the annual figures as seen in the plans."
He did not elaborate but Human has to submit its January-March figures to the Budapest Stock Exchange by May 15.
The company sees its unconsolidated profit rising to 1.2 billion in 1998 and 1.5 billion in 1999 and expects exports to rise to 2.2 billion forints next year from 1.5 billion in 1996.

But one of the main goals of Human is to pass a successful pre-audit by the U.S.'s Food and Drug Administration (FDA), commercial director Lajos Hegedus said, adding that he expected the FDA to visit two of our plants this year.
Speaking about the permormance of Human shares on the bourse last year, Rudolf said price increases pleased the company.
"I think the performance of our shares on the bourse was very positive," he said.
"We are aware of the fact that last year was characterised by very positive market sentiment but I hope that Human's plans form a good base to please shareholders."
Human is majority owned by Canada's Novopharm Ltd.
On the Budapest bourse Human shares closed at 2,980 forints, up 70.
